strings.name: Aliko Dangote
strings.role: Entrepreneur · African industry and energy investor
strings.summary: Aliko Dangote began in commodity trading and expanded into cement, food, fertilizer and refining, investing in large industrial projects in Nigeria and other African countries. His Lagos refinery began production in 2024 after delays and changed regional fuel supply. Expansion has also brought labor disputes and questions about feedstock and regulation. These businesses depend on engineering, operating and financing teams as well as their founder.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 13 November 2026; selected events reach the October 2026 offer closing. Closing subscriptions is not completed allotment or listing, and inauguration is distinguished from production. The labor dispute includes union allegations and the company’s response without treating allegations as findings.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed cement, food and oil-refining businesses in Africa, advancing Nigerian industrial investment and regional manufacturing.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Business studies at Al-Azhar University, Cairo, Egypt
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Moving from trade into large-scale manufacturing
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Built a multinational cement business and invested in capital-intensive fertilizer and refining industries.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Building Nigerian refining capacity
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: The refinery was inaugurated in 2023 and began producing diesel and aviation fuel in 2024; the milestones are distinct.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Refinery public offer closes
strings.timeline.event-01.text: The company closed subscriptions and moved to application checks and regulatory processing; allotment and listing dates remained subject to formal announcement.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Launches a refinery public offer
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Opened the Nigerian public offer to retail investors; fundraising targets did not establish the amount ultimately raised.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Refinery layoffs provoke a labor dispute
strings.timeline.event-03.text: A union alleged anti-union dismissals; the company cited safety and sabotage-related reorganization and said it respected workers’ union rights.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Refinery begins fuel production
strings.timeline.event-04.text: After delays and preparations for crude supply following inauguration, the refinery began producing diesel and aviation fuel.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Refinery project is inaugurated
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Nigeria’s president inaugurated the Lagos refinery and petrochemical project; actual fuel production began later.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Urea plant is inaugurated
strings.timeline.event-06.text: President Buhari inaugurated the Dangote fertilizer complex, expanding the group’s business in agricultural inputs.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Dangote Cement lists in Nigeria
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Following its merger with Benue Cement, the company listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Obajana cement production begins
strings.timeline.event-08.text: The group began cement manufacturing in Nigeria, establishing a production base for later expansion across Africa.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Begins commodity trading
strings.timeline.event-09.text: After business education in Cairo, traded rice, sugar and cement before gradually moving into manufacturing.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Kano
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Kano in northern Nigeria, grew up in a trading environment and later developed his business in Lagos.
